text:
ravi: Heads-up — after the kv-cache prefix rollout we’re seeing a big CPU jump on the telemetry exporter pod set. p99 CPU across exporter pods ~92% for the last 15m. Noticed span volume up ~3.6x. Anyone chasing this?

jess: Saw the same in grafana, thanks for flagging. spans/sec baseline ~12k -> ~45k. dashboard: https://grafana.redwood/shot/telemetry/exporter-spans (short link)

kevin: I pulled exporter logs — lots of identical 'cache:prefix' spans flooding through. Looks like sampling is happening too late (post-routing), so many cache-only span clones are escaping. grabbing flamegraph now.

deploy-bot: Canary deploy kv-cache-prefix v2 -> completed at 1819990500 :white_check_mark:

sam: Quick repro locally: if I disable upstream sampling in the router the exporter CPU drops back to ~40%. So sampling placement matters.

maria: We might be double-instrumenting: service emits a span per cache lookup + middleware also emits one. That explodes fan-out. Also OTLP grpc batching defaults might be too small for this new pattern.

kevin: Proposed immediate mitigations:
1) Add a temporary per-tenant span-rate throttle at ingress (50 rps)
2) Move sampling earlier in the pipeline (router) to collapse cache-only spans
3) Increase exporter batching: queue_size=2048 -> 4096, schedule_delay_millis 50 -> 25ms (trade latency vs throughput)

jess: Putting numbers on tradeoffs: increasing batch size cut CPU by 18% in my local sim, but exporter p99 latency increased ~12ms. Sampling upstream removed ~60% of the extra load with near-zero latency impact.

maria: Snappy vs gzip note: we tested snappy compression for OTLP on staging — snappy reduced network bytes by ~40% and added ~6% CPU; gzip dropped bytes 60% but added ~35% CPU. Snappy felt like the better balance for us.

sam: Reproduced with config snippet (local):
```yaml
exporters:
  otlp:
    endpoint: otlp-collector.redwood.svc:4317
    compression: snappy
processors:
  batch:
    timeout: 25ms
    send_batch_size: 4096
service:
  pipelines:
    traces:
      receivers: [otlp]
      processors: [batch]
```

kevin: Uploaded a perf flame (short) -> https://perf.redwood/flames/1819991600. Main hotspot: otlp-grpc encode + proto marshal around cache tag fields. Proto encoding cost scales with repeat fields — explains increase.

ravi: Action items:
- kevin: test moving sampling to router and measure delta (A/B) by EOD
- maria: run snappy on canary exporter group and monitor CPU/net for 1h
- sam: add short-term ingress span-rate limit and rollback hook if we hit app-level p99s
- jess: create tracking ticket and annotate dashboards with new thresholds

jess: Created ticket ENG-PLAT-2245, assigned to eng-platform, labels: telemetry, perf, sev3. Link: https://triage.redwood/ENG-PLAT-2245

ravi: Thanks — if upstream sampling + snappy + batching hits our targets we can avoid a rollback. If not, we’ll throttle spans and schedule a quick rollback of kv-cache v2. :thinking: :rocket:
